This collection was originally developed for Apptio internal training on the Cloudability API, and has since been modified for general use by Cloudability customers and partners. This can be used as part of learning to interact with the CLDY API suite as well as for day-to-day operations.

## Before You Start

Follow these steps the first time you use this collection:

1. **Import the Environment file** -- import the corresponding environment JSON file into Postman and select it as the active environment
    
2. **Fill in your credentials** -- set `Frontdoor Public` and `Frontdoor Private` in the environment
    
3. **Confirm authentication** -- run the three calls in **000 Authentication > 001 Frontdoor Auth** in order. The test scripts will capture your Opentoken and environment ID, and test your credentials.
    

_Note: Other calls may use variables that need to be populated before you run them. Some of the calls have scripts that capture values and populate variables automatically (see below). Check all variables that are referenced in calls to ensure they have the expected values before running._

> **Quick start with a long-lived API key:** Set `cldykey` = your API key, and `skip_auto_auth=true`. You'll need to change the Auth method on all calls to use this authentication method, so this is not recommended.

item.name: 000 Authentication
001 Frontdoor AuthN (OpenToken)

request.description:
**POST** `https://frontdoor.apptio.com/service/apikeylogin`

Exchanges a Frontdoor API key pair for a short-lived OpenToken (session bearer token). The token is returned as a **response cookie** named `apptio-opentoken` and is valid for **30 minutes**.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
| `Accept` | `application/json` |

### Request Body

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `keyAccess` | The **public key** from your Frontdoor API key pair. Store as `{{Frontdoor Public}}` |
| `keySecret` | The **secret key** from your Frontdoor API key pair. Store as `{{Frontdoor Secret}}` |

### How to Create API Keys

1. In **Access Administration**, open the User or Service Account record
2. Create a new API key pair — choose **No Expiration** or **90-day Expiration**
3. The account must have at minimum **Cloudability Admin** permission
4. Save the Public and Secret values into your Postman environment

### Test Script

This collection automatically captures the returned token:

``` javascript
var t = postman.getResponseCookie("apptio-opentoken").value;
pm.environment.set("apptio-opentoken", t);
```

_The token expires after 30 minutes. Re-run this call to get a fresh token._

**GET** `https://frontdoor.apptio.com/api/environment/{domain}/{environmentName}` Returns the Apptio **Environment ID** (`apptio-current-environment`) for the specified domain and environment. This value is required as a header on every subsequent Cloudability API call. ### Required Headers | Header | Value | | --- | --- | | `apptio-opentoken` | Token from step 1. Use `{{apptio-opentoken}}` | ### Path Variables | Variable | Description | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | `{{domain}}` | Your organization's Apptio domain | `acme.com` | | `{{environment-name}}` | The Apptio environment name | `main` | ### Response The response body contains an `id` field — this is your permanent `apptio-current-environment` value. ### Test Script ``` javascript var jsonData = pm.response.json(); pm.environment.set("apptio-current-environment", jsonData.id); ``` _**This call only needs to be made once.**_ _The Environment ID is permanent and never changes for a given Cloudability instance._

item.description:
Frontdoor Authentication is the standard across all Apptio/IBM products. It follows a key pair/OpenToken methodology: a public and private key attached to a User or Service Account in Access Administration are exchanged for a short-lived OpenToken (bearer token). This token, combined with a permanent Environment ID, authenticates all Cloudability API v3 calls for 30 minutes.

### Steps

1. **Create API keys** in Access Administration against a User or Service Account
   - Choose **No Expiration** or **90-day Expiration**
   - The key must have at least **Cloudability Admin** permission
   - Keys cannot exceed the permission level of the account they belong to

2. **Get OpenToken** (call 1) — POST your key pair to receive the `apptio-opentoken` cookie (valid 30 min)

3. **Get Environment ID** (call 2) — retrieve the permanent `apptio-current-environment` value once

4. **Use both as headers** on every subsequent Cloudability API call

5. After 30 minutes, re-run call 1 to refresh the token. The Environment ID never needs to be re-fetched.

_Reference: [Frontdoor API Key Authentication](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/apptio-platform/access-administration/saas?topic=apis-authentication-via-api-keys)_

item.description:
### Generating a Cloudability API Key

1. Log in to Cloudability
    
2. Navigate to **Settings > API Access** (Admins only)
    
3. Generate or copy your API key
    
4. Use the key as the Basic Auth username with an empty password
    

Note: The use of this authentication method is demonstrated in the child "Call Endpoint (Organizations)" call. All other API calls in this collection use the preferred authentication method (Opentoken). This can be changed in any call by updating the **Authorization** tab (Basic Auth with the Cloudability Key specified the Username) and unchecking the following from the **Headers** tab:

- apptio-opentoken
    
- apptio-current-environment

This section covers the [two types of authentication](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-getting-started-cloudability-v3) supported by the Cloudability API v3.

### API Key Management and Rotation

**Two authentication methods** are supported by Cloudability API v3:

1. **Frontdoor Authentication** (001) is the standard method across all Apptio/IBM products
    

- A public/private key pair is generated in Access Administration. API keys can be set to **No Expiration** or **90-day Expiration**
    
- This key pair is used to obtain a short-lived Opentoken that, when paired with a permanent Environment ID, authenticates API calls
    
- The Opentoken is a short-lived bearer token which expires and must be refreshed after 30 minutes
    

2\. Cloudability Key Authentication (002) uses a per-user bearer token with HTTP Basic Authentication

- **This method has been deprecated in favor of Frontdoor Authentication, and should not be used for production calls**
    
- A long-lived key generated directly within Cloudability
    
- Passed as a Basic Auth username with an empty password (using the `-u 'apikey:'` curl pattern)
    

### Token / Key Expiry

| Type | Expiry Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Frontdoor OpenToken | Short-lived -- expires after a set period (typically hours). Refresh by re-running the 001 Auth flow. |
| Cloudability API Key | Long-lived -- does not expire automatically, but can be revoked or regenerated at any time from Settings > API Access. |

### When Authentication Fails

If any API call returns **HTTP 401 Unauthorized**, the most common causes are:

| Cause | Resolution |
| --- | --- |
| OpenToken expired | Re-run the **1\. Get OpenToken** call in section 001 and update `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| API key revoked or regenerated | Retrieve the new key from **Settings > API Access** and update the environment variable |
| Wrong environment ID | Verify `{{apptio-current-environment}}` matches your org's environment ID (run **2\. Get Environment ID**) |
| Insufficient permissions | Confirm the user account associated with the API key has the required Cloudability permissions for the operation |

### Security Best Practices

- Store API keys and tokens as **secret** variables in your Postman Environment (marked `type: secret`) -- never paste them into call headers directly
    
- Do not commit API keys to source control -- use environment variable injection in CI/CD pipelines
    
- Rotate Cloudability API keys periodically from **Settings > API Access**
    
- For service account automation, use a dedicated Cloudability service user rather than a personal account's API key
    

---

### Disabling Automatic Token Refresh (`skip_auto_auth`)

The collection includes a **pre-request script** that automatically refreshes your Frontdoor OpenToken before every call when it detects the token is expired or missing. If you prefer to manage authentication manually — for example when using a **long-lived Cloudability API key** instead of Frontdoor tokens — you can disable the auto-refresh:

**To disable auto-refresh:**

1. Open your **Cloudability API v3 Environment**
    
2. Set the variable: `skip_auto_auth` = `true`
    
3. The pre-request script will skip token refresh for every call in the collection
    

**To re-enable auto-refresh:**

- Set `skip_auto_auth` to `false`
    

**When to use** **`skip_auto_auth=true`****:**

| Scenario | Recommendation |
| --- | --- |
| Using Frontdoor OpenToken and want auto-refresh | Leave unset or set to `false` |
| Testing authentication flows manually via the 001 calls | Set `skip_auto_auth=true` to prevent the script from running first |
| CI/CD pipeline with pre-injected token | Set `skip_auto_auth=true` to prevent credential prompting |

> **Note:** When `skip_auto_auth=true`, the `apptio-opentoken` environment variable must be set manually and kept current. If it expires and no auto-refresh occurs, all API calls will return **HTTP 401 Unauthorized**.

query.description: 0 = all accounts; use a View ID to scope to a specific view

request.description:
**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/vendors/aws/accounts`

Returns a list of all AWS accounts currently credentialed in Cloudability, including their credential status, account type (master payer or linked), and associated metadata.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Query Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `viewid` | No | Scope results to a specific View. `0` returns all accounts regardless of view | `viewid=0` |

### Response Fields (per account)

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `vendorAccountId` | The AWS Account ID (12-digit) |
| `type` | Credential type: `aws_role` (IAM Role) or `aws_key` (Access Key) |
| `verification` | Current verification status (`verified`, `failed`, `pending`) |
| `parentAccountId` | For linked accounts, the master payer account ID |
| `roleName` | Name of the IAM role used (for `aws_role` type) |
| `externalId` | The External ID configured in the IAM trust policy |

**POST** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/vendors/aws/accounts`

Adds a new AWS account credential to Cloudability. This initiates the credentialing process for an AWS account so that Cloudability can begin ingesting its cost and usage data.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Request Body

| Field | Required | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | Yes | Credential type. Use `aws_role` for IAM Role (recommended) or `aws_key` for Access Key | `"aws_role"` |
| `vendorAccountId` | Yes | The 12-digit AWS Account ID to credential | `"123456789012"` |

### IAM Role Prerequisites (for `aws_role` type)

Before calling this endpoint, an IAM Role named `CloudabilityRole` (or your custom name) must exist in the target AWS account with:
- A trust policy granting the Cloudability AWS account permission to assume the role
- The External ID provided by Cloudability set in the trust policy
- The `ReadOnlyAccess` managed policy (or equivalent billing read permissions) attached

### Query Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `viewid` | Scope to a specific View. Use `0` for all accounts |

_After creation, use **Verify Accounts** to confirm Cloudability can successfully assume the role and ingest data._

Updates the IAM Role name or External ID for an existing **linked** (member) AWS account credential. Use this when you have rotated the External ID in your IAM trust policy or renamed the IAM role in the target account.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Path Variables

| Variable | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `{{vendorAccountId}}` | The 12-digit AWS Account ID of the linked account to update | `"123456789012"` |

### Request Body

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | Yes | Must be `"aws_role"` |
| `roleName` | Yes | The IAM role name in the target account (default: `CloudabilityRole`) |
| `externalId` | Yes | The External ID set in the IAM trust policy |
| `parentAccountId` | No | The master payer account ID this linked account belongs to |

|---|---|

item.name: Change Master Account External ID or Role Name

request.description:
**PUT** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/vendors/AWS/accounts/{vendorAccountId}`

Updates the IAM Role name or External ID for an existing **master payer** AWS account credential. Use this when you have rotated the External ID in your IAM trust policy or renamed the IAM role on the payer account.

This call uses the same endpoint as the linked account update — the distinction is that the `vendorAccountId` in the path refers to the **master payer account**, not a linked account.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Path Variables

| Variable | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `{{vendorAccountId}}` | The 12-digit AWS Account ID of the **master payer** account | `"111122223333"` |

### Request Body

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | Yes | Must be `"aws_role"` |
| `roleName` | Yes | The IAM role name in the master account (default: `CloudabilityRole`) |
| `externalId` | Yes | The External ID configured in the IAM trust policy |
| `parentAccountId` | No | For organizational hierarchy reference; typically the same as `vendorAccountId` for a payer |

_After updating, run **Verify Accounts** to confirm the updated credentials are valid._

**POST** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/vendors/aws/accounts` _(with verification payload)_

Triggers Cloudability to attempt to assume the IAM role for the specified AWS account and validates that the credential is correctly configured. This is the recommended step after creating or updating any AWS credential.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Request Body

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | Yes | Credential type: `"aws_role"` or `"aws_key"` |
| `vendorAccountId` | Yes | The 12-digit AWS Account ID to verify |

### Verification Status Values

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `verified` | Cloudability successfully connected to the account |
| `failed` | The credential is invalid — check the IAM role trust policy and permissions |
| `pending` | Verification is in progress; check again shortly |

_Common failure causes: incorrect External ID, role name mismatch, missing billing permissions, or the IAM role does not exist in the target account._

item.description:
## AWS Vendor Credentials

This sub-folder covers the full lifecycle of managing AWS account credentials in Cloudability via the [Vendor Credentials API](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-vendor-credentials-end-point-aws).

Cloudability uses **IAM Role assumption** (recommended) or **IAM Access Keys** to connect to AWS accounts and ingest Cost and Usage Report (CUR) data.

### Typical Workflow

1. **Create Account Credential** — register an AWS account in Cloudability
2. **Verify Accounts** — confirm Cloudability can successfully connect
3. **Change External ID or Role Name** — use if you rotate credentials or rename the IAM role
4. **Get AWS Accounts** — list all credentialed accounts and their current status

### IAM Role Setup (one-time, per AWS account)

Before credentialing, create an IAM Role in each target AWS account with:
- **Role name:** `CloudabilityRole` (or a custom name you specify in the API)
- **Trust policy:** Allow the Cloudability AWS account to assume the role, with the Cloudability-provided External ID
- **Permissions:** AWS managed policy `ReadOnlyAccess` plus `billing:*` for the payer account

### Key Concepts

- **Master Payer Account:** The AWS Organizations payer account that holds consolidated billing. This account must have the IAM role and access to the CUR S3 bucket.
- **Linked Accounts:** Member accounts within an AWS Organization. Each can also be individually credentialed for tag and resource-level data.
- **`viewid` parameter:** Present on most calls. Use `0` to operate across all accounts, or provide a specific View ID to scope the operation.

Creates a new Azure credential in Cloudability by associating an **Enrollment ID** with an authentication location (the Azure billing export storage path). This is typically used for Enterprise Agreement (EA) customers connecting via Azure Billing API.

### Prerequisites

Before calling this endpoint:
- Your Azure EA enrollment must be active
- The API key (from the Azure EA portal) must be available
- For modern MCA/CSP setups, refer to the Cloudability UI for the recommended setup flow

_After creating the credential, use **Verify** to confirm connectivity._

### Verification Status Values

|---|---|
| `verified` | Cloudability successfully authenticated to Azure |
| `failed` | The credential is invalid — check the API key or service principal permissions |
| `pending` | Verification is queued; check again shortly |

## Azure Vendor Credentials

This sub-folder covers managing Azure account credentials in Cloudability via the [Vendor Credentials API](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-vendor-credentials-end-point-aws).

Cloudability supports Azure **Enterprise Agreement (EA)** enrollments and individual **Subscriptions**. The credentialing method depends on your Azure agreement type:

| Agreement Type | Credential Method |
|---|---|
| Enterprise Agreement (EA) | Enrollment ID + EA API key via `auth-locations` |
| Microsoft Customer Agreement (MCA) | Service Principal + Billing Export to Storage |
| Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) | Service Principal + Partner Center API |

### Typical Workflow

1. **Get Accounts** — list all currently credentialed Azure accounts and their status
2. **Create CLDY Credential** — register a new EA Enrollment ID with its authentication location
3. **Verify** — confirm Cloudability can successfully connect to the Azure account

### Key Concepts

- **Enrollment ID:** The unique identifier for an Azure Enterprise Agreement, found in the Azure EA Portal
- **Subscription ID:** A UUID identifying a specific Azure Subscription (`xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx`)
- **`viewId` parameter:** Use `0` to operate across all accounts, or provide a View ID to scope the operation

item.name: 053 GCP Credentials

query.description: 0 = all accounts; use a View ID to scope results

request.description:
**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/vendors/gcp/accounts`

Returns a list of all Google Cloud Platform (GCP) projects and billing accounts currently credentialed in Cloudability, including their verification status and configuration metadata.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Query Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `viewid` | No | Scope results to a specific View. `0` returns all GCP accounts | `viewid=0` |

### Response Fields (per account)

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `vendorAccountId` | The GCP Project ID or Billing Account ID |
| `type` | Credential type (e.g., `gcp_service_account`) |
| `verification` | Current status: `verified`, `failed`, or `pending` |
| `displayName` | The GCP project or account display name |

### GCP Credentialing Prerequisites

GCP accounts are credentialed using a **Service Account** with the following setup:
- A GCP Service Account with **Viewer** and **BigQuery Data Viewer** roles
- Billing data exported to a **BigQuery dataset**
- The Service Account's JSON key uploaded to Cloudability (via UI or API)

_Note: The original collection URL for this call pointed to the Azure endpoint — this has been corrected to the GCP endpoint (`/vendors/gcp/accounts`)._

query.description: View scope (0 = all data)

variable.description: GCP Billing Account ID -- retrieve from Get GCP Accounts

request.description:
**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/vendors/gcp/accounts/:accountId/setup-scripts`

Returns a ready-to-run **gcloud CLI script** that creates the Cloudability IAM role and assigns the minimum required BigQuery and Cloud Billing permissions to a Service Account in your GCP project. This is the fastest way to configure a new GCP project for Cloudability ingestion without manually looking up required permissions.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Path Parameter

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `:accountId` | GCP Billing Account ID registered in Cloudability | `01A1DD-D1F1E1-F11111` |

### Query Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `viewId` | No | Scope to a View (use `0` for all data) | `0` |

### Example Request

```
GET https://api.cloudability.com/v3/vendors/gcp/accounts/01A1DD-D1F1E1-F11111/setup-scripts?viewId=0
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "scripts": "gcloud iam roles create CloudabilityRole_Billing \
      --project sampleproject \
      --title \"Cloudability Billing Role\" \
      --description \"Allows Cloudability access to billing account data\" \
      --permissions bigquery.jobs.create,bigquery.tables.getData, ..."
  }
}
```

### Workflow

1. Call **Get GCP Accounts** to find the `accountId` for the project you want to set up
2. Call **Get GCP Setup Script** -- copy the `result.scripts` value
3. Run the script in your GCP Cloud Shell or a local terminal with `gcloud` configured
4. After the script runs, call **Create GCP Account Credential** to register the project
5. Call **Verify GCP Account** to confirm connectivity

### Notes

- The script is generated specifically for the account ID provided -- do not reuse one script across multiple projects
- The generated script requires the `gcloud` CLI to be installed and authenticated with an account that has `roles/iam.roleAdmin` and `roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin` permissions on the target project
- _Reference: [Vendor Credentials Endpoints (GCP)](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-vendor-credentials-end-points-gcp)_

**POST** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/vendors/gcp/accounts`

Creates a new GCP project credential in Cloudability using the **GCP IAM Role** method. This call registers a GCP project's billing export configuration so Cloudability can ingest cost and usage data.

> **Prerequisite:** Before calling this endpoint, complete the GCP setup steps described in the 053 folder -- BigQuery billing export enabled, IAM role created, and the Service Account configured with the correct permissions.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |

### Request Body Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vendorAccountId` | string | Yes | GCP Billing Account ID (format: `XXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXX`) |
| `type` | string | Yes | Credential type -- use `gcp_role` for IAM Role method; `gcp_byod_role` for BYOD |
| `tableFqn` | string | Yes | Fully qualified BigQuery table name for billing export (`project:dataset.table`) |
| `consumerOrgId` | string | No | GCP Organization ID -- leave empty if not applicable |
| `bucketName` | string | No | GCS bucket name for exported billing data |
| `isResourceLevelBillingRequired` | boolean | No | Set `true` to enable resource-level billing detail |
| `rlbdate` | string | No | Start date for resource-level billing (`YYYY-MM-DD`) |
| `gcpOrgId` | string | No | GCP Organization ID for org-level billing accounts |

### Example Request Body

```json
{
  "vendorAccountId": "01A1DD-D1F1E1-F11111",
  "type": "gcp_role",
  "tableFqn": "myproject:billing_dataset.gcp_billing_export_v1_01A1DD-D1F1E1-F11111",
  "consumerOrgId": "",
  "bucketName": "",
  "isResourceLevelBillingRequired": false,
  "rlbdate": "",
  "gcpOrgId": ""
}
```

### Response

A successful response returns a `result` object with the registered account details including `id`, `vendorAccountId`, `vendorAccountName`, and the linked BigQuery configuration.

### Notes

- After creating the credential, use **Verify GCP Account** to confirm Cloudability can access the BigQuery export
- The `tableFqn` must exactly match the BigQuery export table name created during GCP setup
- For BYOD (Bring Your Own Data) integrations, use `type: gcp_byod_role` instead
- _Reference: [Vendor Credentials Endpoints (GCP)](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-vendor-credentials-end-points-gcp)_

**POST** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/vendors/gcp/accounts/verify`

Verifies that Cloudability can successfully connect to and read from the GCP BigQuery billing export for one or more registered GCP accounts. Run this after creating a new GCP credential or after changing IAM permissions.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |

### Request Body Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vendorAccountIds` | array | Yes | Array of GCP Billing Account IDs to verify (e.g., `["01A1DD-D1F1E1-F11111"]`) |

### Example Request Body

```json
{
  "vendorAccountIds": ["01A1DD-D1F1E1-F11111"]
}
```

### Verification States

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `verified` | Cloudability can access the BigQuery export -- data ingestion is active |
| `pending` | Verification in progress -- check again shortly |
| `failed` | Access check failed -- review IAM permissions and BigQuery export configuration |

### Common Failure Reasons

- The Service Account does not have **BigQuery Data Viewer** or **BigQuery Job User** roles on the dataset project
- The `tableFqn` provided during account creation is incorrect or the table does not yet exist
- Cloud Billing export to BigQuery has not yet generated data (new billing accounts can take 24-48 hours)
- Cross-project permission is missing when the BigQuery dataset lives in a different project from the billing account

### Notes

- Verification checks connectivity only -- allow 24-48 hours after first setup for billing data to appear in Cloudability dashboards
- _Reference: [Vendor Credentials Endpoints (GCP)](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-vendor-credentials-end-points-gcp)_

## GCP Vendor Credentials

This sub-folder covers managing Google Cloud Platform (GCP) account credentials in Cloudability via the [Vendor Credentials API](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-vendor-credentials-end-point-aws).

Cloudability connects to GCP using a **Service Account** with access to a **BigQuery billing export dataset**. The exported billing data is the source of all GCP cost and usage information in Cloudability.

### GCP Setup Summary

1. In GCP, enable **Cloud Billing export to BigQuery** on your Billing Account
2. Create a **Service Account** in the GCP project that holds the BigQuery dataset
3. Grant the Service Account the **BigQuery Data Viewer** and **BigQuery Job User** roles on the dataset project
4. Grant the Service Account the **Billing Account Viewer** role on the Billing Account
5. Download the Service Account JSON key
6. Upload the key to Cloudability (via the UI **Accounts** page or API)

### Notes

- GCP Rightsizing uses `basis=on-demand` — there is no `effective` cost basis for GCP
- The `viewid` parameter scopes results to a specific Cloudability View (`0` = all)
- Additional GCP credentialing calls are now included in this sub-folder -- see **Create GCP Account Credential** and **Verify GCP Account** below.s

### API-Assisted Setup

Use the **Get GCP Setup Script** call in this sub-folder to retrieve a pre-generated `gcloud` CLI script that creates the Cloudability IAM role with the correct permissions for a registered GCP billing account. This eliminates the need to look up individual permission names manually.

request.description:
**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/business-mappings`

Returns all Business Dimension mappings defined in the Cloudability instance. Each mapping includes its unique `index`, name, default value, and all configured match/value statement pairs.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Response Fields (per mapping)

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `index` | Unique numeric identifier for the mapping — use this in PUT/DELETE calls and as `category{index}` in Cost Reporting |
| `name` | The display name of the Business Dimension as it appears in reports |
| `defaultValue` | The value assigned to any line item that does not match any statement |
| `statements` | Array of match/value expression pairs evaluated top-to-bottom |
| `statements[].matchExpression` | Boolean expression evaluated against billing line item attributes |
| `statements[].valueExpression` | The value assigned to the dimension when the matchExpression is true |

_Tip: Note each mapping's `index` value — you will need it to retrieve, update, or delete a specific mapping. The `index` also determines the `category#` dimension name used in Cost Reporting (e.g., `index: 2` → `category2`)._

**POST** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/business-mappings`

Creates a new Business Dimension mapping. Cloudability evaluates the `statements` array top-to-bottom against every billing line item — the first matching statement's `valueExpression` is used. If no statement matches, the `defaultValue` is applied.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Request Body Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Yes | Display name for the Business Dimension (appears in reports as this name) |
| `defaultValue` | Yes | Value assigned to line items that match no statement |
| `statements` | Yes | Array of match/value expression pairs (evaluated in order) |
| `statements[].matchExpression` | Yes | A boolean expression using `DIMENSION[...]`, `METRIC[...]`, `TAG[...]` etc. |
| `statements[].valueExpression` | Yes | The string value to assign when the match is true |

### Expression Language Examples

| Expression | What it matches |
| --- | --- |
| `DIMENSION['availability_zone'] == 'us-east-1'` | A specific AWS availability zone |
| `DIMENSION['vendor'] == 'Amazon'` | All AWS line items |
| `TAG['Environment'] == 'Production'` | A specific tag value |
| `DIMENSION['account_identifier'] =~ '1234.\*'` | Account IDs matching a regex |

### Example Request Body

``` json
{
    "name": "AZ",
    "defaultValue": "south or north",
    "statements": [
        {
            "matchExpression": "DIMENSION['availability_zone'] == 'us-east-1'",
            "valueExpression": "'East'"
        },
        {
            "matchExpression": "DIMENSION['availability_zone'] == 'us-west-1'",
            "valueExpression": "'West'"
        }
    ]
}

 ```

_The_ `_index_` _for the new mapping is auto-assigned by Cloudability and returned in the response. Record it for use in subsequent PUT/DELETE calls._

**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/business-mappings/{index}` Returns the full definition of a single Business Dimension mapping identified by its `index`. Use this before a PUT to retrieve the current state of a mapping (since PUT is a full overwrite, you must include all existing statements you want to keep). ### Required Headers | Header | Value | |---|---| | `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` | | `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` | ### Path Parameter | Parameter | Description | Example | |---|---|---| | `{index}` | The numeric index of the mapping. Find it by running **Retrieve Business Mappings** | `8` | ### How to Find the Index Call **Retrieve Business Mappings** (GET all) first — each mapping object contains an `index` field: For example, if the mapping you want has `"index": 2`, call: `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/business-mappings/2`

**PUT** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/business-mappings/{index}`

Fully replaces an existing Business Dimension mapping with the supplied request body.

> ⚠️ **THIS IS A FULL OVERWRITE AND CANNOT BE REVERTED.** The entire mapping — including all statements — is replaced with exactly what you send. Any statements not included in the request body will be permanently deleted. 
  

### Best Practice

Always call **Retrieve a Specific Business Mapping** (GET by index) first to obtain the current state, then modify that response body and send it as the PUT payload to avoid accidentally dropping statements.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Path Parameter

| Parameter | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{index}` | The numeric index of the mapping to update | `8` |

### Request Body

Same structure as POST (Create). Must include `name`, `defaultValue`, and the **complete** `statements` array reflecting the desired final state.

**DELETE** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/business-mappings/{index}`

Permanently deletes the Business Dimension mapping with the specified index.

> ⚠️ **THIS ACTION CANNOT BE REVERTED.** Once deleted, the mapping and all its statements are gone. Any reports or dashboards using this Business Dimension as `category{index}` will lose that dimension.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Path Parameter

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `{index}` | The numeric index of the mapping to delete | `8` |

_Tip: Run **Retrieve Business Mappings** first to confirm the correct index before deleting._

item.description:
## Business Mappings

_Reference: [Business Mappings Endpoint](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-business-mappings-end-point)_

**Business Mapping** allows you to map cloud cost and usage data to custom dimensions (**Business Dimensions**) and custom metrics (**Business Metrics**) that are meaningful to your organization — beyond what native cloud tagging provides.

### Business Dimensions

Business Dimensions are synthetic dimensions created via Business Mapping statements. They behave like vendor tags but are far more flexible: you can derive their values from any combination of existing dimensions, tags, account identifiers, or cost values. In Cost Reporting, Business Dimensions appear as `category{index}` (e.g., the mapping with `index: 2` is available as dimension `category2`).

### How Business Mapping Works

When Cloudability ingests billing data, each line item is evaluated against the `matchExpressions` in every Business Mapping — top to bottom, like a case statement. The first matching statement's `valueExpression` is used. If no statement matches, the `defaultValue` is applied.

### Workflow

1. **Retrieve Business Mappings** — list all existing mappings and find their `index` values
2. **Create a Business Mapping** — define a new Business Dimension with its statement rules
3. **Retrieve a Specific Business Mapping** — fetch the current state before making changes
4. **Update a Business Mapping** — fully replace a mapping's definition (full overwrite — include all statements)
5. **Delete a Business Mapping** — permanently remove a mapping (irreversible)

### Important Notes

- PUT is a **full overwrite** — always retrieve the existing mapping before updating
- The `index` value is auto-assigned on creation and is permanent
- Business Dimensions appear in Cost Reporting as `category{index}` (e.g., `category2`, `category5`)
- For Business Metrics (numeric synthetic metrics), see section **150 Business Metrics**

_For GUI-based Business Dimension management, see the Cloudability Admin interface under **Allocate > Business Mappings**._

request.description:
**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/business-mappings/metrics`

Returns all Business Metric definitions configured in the Cloudability instance. Each metric includes its unique `index`, name, number format, default value expression, and statement rules.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Response Fields (per metric)

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `index` | Unique numeric identifier — use in GET/PUT/DELETE calls by index |
| `name` | Display name for the metric as it appears in reports |
| `numberFormat` | How the value is formatted: `currency`, `number`, or `percentage` |
| `defaultValueExpression` | Numeric expression applied when no statement matches (note: `Expression` suffix is required) |
| `statements` | Array of match/value expression pairs evaluated top-to-bottom |
| `statements[].matchExpression` | Boolean expression against billing line item attributes |
| `statements[].valueExpression` | Numeric expression (can reference `METRIC[...]`) assigned when match is true |

_Note: Record each metric's `index` — you need it to retrieve, update, or delete a specific metric._

**POST** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/internal/business-mappings/metrics`

Creates a new Business Metric. Business Metrics are numeric synthetic metrics derived from billing data using match/value statement rules — useful for modeling taxes, showback rates, RI/SP savings, and custom cost allocations.

> **Note:** Business Metrics use the `/v3/internal/` path prefix, unlike Business Dimensions which use `/v3/`.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Request Body Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Yes | Display name for the metric |
| `defaultValueExpression` | Yes | ⚠️ Must use the word **`Expression`** — the API will fail if you use `defaultValue` |
| `numberFormat` | Yes | `"currency"`, `"number"`, or `"percentage"` |
| `statements` | Yes | Array of match/value pairs (evaluated top-to-bottom) |
| `statements[].matchExpression` | Yes | Boolean expression (same syntax as Business Dimensions) |
| `statements[].valueExpression` | Yes | A **numeric** expression — can reference other metrics via `METRIC['metric_name']` |

### valueExpression Examples

| Expression | Description |
|---|---|
| `METRIC['unblended_cost'] * 1.10` | Add 10% surcharge to unblended cost |
| `METRIC['cost_amortized'] * 0.05` | 5% of amortized cost |
| `METRIC['usage_hours'] * 0.25` | Flat rate per usage hour |

### Common Referenceable Metrics

`unblended_cost`, `cost_amortized`, `usage_hours`, `total_amortized_cost`

**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/internal/business-mappings/{index}/metrics` Returns the full definition of a single Business Metric identified by its `index`. Use this before a PUT to capture the current state — since PUT is a full overwrite, you must include all existing statements you want to retain. ### Required Headers | Header | Value | |---|---| | `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` | | `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` | ### Path Parameter | Parameter | Description | Example | |---|---|---| | `{index}` | The numeric index of the Business Metric. Find it via **Retrieve Business Metrics** | `5` | ### How to Find the Index Call **Retrieve Business Metrics** (GET all) first — each metric object contains an `index` field: For example, for a metric with `"index": 5`, call: `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/internal/business-mappings/5/metrics`

**PUT** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/internal/business-mappings/{index}/metrics`

Fully replaces an existing Business Metric with the supplied request body.

> ⚠️ **THIS IS A FULL OVERWRITE AND CANNOT BE REVERTED.** All existing statements are replaced with exactly what you send. Any statements omitted from the request body will be permanently lost.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Path Parameter

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `{index}` | The numeric index of the metric to update | `5` |

### Request Body

Same structure as POST (Create). Must include `name`, `defaultValueExpression` (not `defaultValue`), `numberFormat`, and the **complete** `statements` array.

_Best practice: retrieve the metric first (GET by index), modify the response body, then submit the full modified payload as the PUT body._

**DELETE** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/internal/business-mappings/{index}/metrics`

Permanently deletes the Business Metric with the specified index.

> ⚠️ **THIS ACTION CANNOT BE REVERTED.** The metric is permanently removed. Any reports using this metric will no longer be able to reference it.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Path Parameter

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `{index}` | The numeric index of the metric to delete | `5` |

_Run **Retrieve Business Metrics** first to confirm the correct index._

## Business Metrics

_Reference: [Business Mappings Endpoint](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-business-mappings-end-point)_

Business Metrics are **numeric synthetic metrics** created through Business Mapping statements. Unlike Business Dimensions (which produce string/categorical values), Business Metrics produce numeric outputs that can be reported on in dashboards and exports — useful for modeling surcharges, showback rates, RI/SP savings calculations, and custom cost allocations.

> **This API is the only way to manage Business Metrics. There is no UI in Cloudability to create, modify, or delete them.**

> **Internal API Path Warning:** Business Metrics use the path `/v3/internal/business-mappings/metrics` -- note the `/internal/` segment. This path is **not listed in the IBM Cloudability public API documentation**. While it is accessible with a valid API key, it may change without notice in future Cloudability releases and is not covered by IBM's standard API backward-compatibility guarantees. Test in a non-production environment first and monitor your automation after each Cloudability platform update.

### Key Differences from Business Dimensions (Section 100)

| | Business Dimensions | Business Metrics |
|---|---|---|
| Output type | String/categorical | Numeric |
| API path | `/v3/business-mappings` | `/v3/internal/business-mappings/metrics` |
| Body field | `defaultValue` | `defaultValueExpression` |
| Use in reports | `category{index}` dimension | Named metric |

### Workflow

1. **Retrieve Business Metrics** — list all existing metrics and note their `index` values
2. **Create a Business Metric** — define rules using `matchExpression` / `valueExpression` pairs
3. **Retrieve a Specific Business Metric** — fetch current state before any update
4. **Update a Business Metric** — fully replace the metric definition (full overwrite)
5. **Delete a Business Metric** — permanently remove a metric (irreversible)

### Important Notes

- The request body field **must be `defaultValueExpression`** (not `defaultValue`) — the API returns an error otherwise
- `valueExpression` must be a **numeric** expression; you can reference standard metrics using `METRIC['metric_name']`
- Metrics use the `/v3/internal/` path prefix
- PUT is a **full overwrite** — retrieve the metric first before updating

**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/account_groups`

Returns all Account Groups defined in the Cloudability instance. Account Groups are key/value groupings applied to cloud accounts — the group name is the key (e.g., "Environment") and Account Group Entries provide the values (e.g., "Production", "Development").

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |

| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

| Field | Description |

| `id` | Unique numeric identifier for the Account Group — use in PUT and DELETE calls |
| `name` | The Account Group name as it appears as a reporting dimension throughout Cloudability |
| `position` | The display order of this group relative to others |
| `account_group_entry_values` | Summary list of distinct values currently assigned via Account Group Entries |

_Record the `id` of each Account Group — you need it for update, delete, and when creating Account Group Entries._

**POST** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/account_groups`

Creates a new Account Group. This defines the **key** (dimension name) that will appear throughout Cloudability reporting. After creating the group, use **Account Group Entries** (section 202) to assign values to specific cloud accounts.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Request Body Fields

| Field | Required | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Yes | The Account Group name — appears as a reporting dimension in all Cloudability views | `"Environment"` |
| `position` | Yes | Display order among all Account Groups (lower numbers appear first) | `1` |

### Example Request Bodies

``` json
{ "name": "Environment", "position": 1 }
{ "name": "Cost Center", "position": 2 }
{ "name": "Team", "position": 3 }

 ```

_The_ `_id_` _of the new Account Group is returned in the response. Record it for use in Account Group Entry calls._

**PUT** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/account_groups/{id}`

Updates the name or position of an existing Account Group. This renames the reporting dimension across all Cloudability views and reports.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Path Parameter

| Parameter | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{id}` | The numeric ID of the Account Group to update. Find it via **Get Account Groups** | `6720` |

### Request Body Fields

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | New display name for the Account Group |
| `position` | Display order position |

_Note: Updating the name of an Account Group renames the reporting dimension everywhere it is used in Cloudability._

**DELETE** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/account_groups/{id}`

> ⚠️ **Deleting an Account Group also deletes all Account Group Entries assigned to it.** This action cannot be undone.

## Account Groups

_Reference: [Account Groups Endpoint](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-account-groups-end-point)_

Account Groups function as a tagging system for cloud accounts (AWS accounts, Azure Subscriptions, GCP Projects) at the Cloudability level — independent of native cloud tags. They define a **key** (the group name, e.g., "Environment") that becomes a reporting dimension throughout Cloudability.

**Account Group Entries** (section 202) are used to assign **values** to specific accounts within a group (e.g., AWS account `123456789012` → `Production`).

### Account Groups Object Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | number | Unique identifier — used in PUT, DELETE, and Entry creation |
| `name` | string | The dimension name as it appears in reports |
| `position` | number | Display order among all Account Groups |
| `account_group_entry_values` | array | Read-only summary of distinct values currently assigned |

### Workflow

1. **Get Account Groups** — list all existing groups and find their `id` values
2. **Create Account Group** — define a new key/dimension
3. **Update Account Group** — rename or reorder an existing group
4. **Delete Account Group** — remove the group and all its entries (irreversible)
5. Then use **202 Account Group Entries** to assign account-level values

_Only Admins can create, update, and delete Account Groups. All users can access the generated dimensions in dashboards and reports._

item.description:
## Account Group Entries

_Reference: [Account Group Entries Endpoint](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-account-group-entries)_

Account Group Entries are the **values** side of the Account Group key/value system. Each entry assigns a specific cloud account (by its account identifier) to a value within a given Account Group.

**Example:** For an Account Group named `"Environment"` (id: 6720), you create entries like:
- AWS account `123456789012` → `"Production"`
- AWS account `987654321098` → `"Development"`
- Azure subscription `xxxxxxxx-xxxx` → `"Staging"`

Once assigned, users can filter and group cost reports by `"Environment"` = `"Production"` etc.

### Account Group Entry Object Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | number | Unique identifier for the entry — used in PUT and DELETE calls |
| `account_group_id` | number | ID of the parent Account Group (from section 201) |
| `account_identifier` | string | Cloud account ID: AWS Account ID, Azure Subscription ID, or GCP Project ID |
| `value` | string | The value assigned to this account within the Account Group |

### Workflow

1. **Account Group Entries** (GET) — list all existing entries across all groups
2. **Create Account Group Entry** — assign a value to a cloud account for a specific group
3. **Update Account Group Entry** — change the value assigned to an existing entry
4. **Delete Account Group Entry** — remove the assignment for a specific account

### Bulk Operations Note

For large-scale Account Group Entry management (e.g., tagging hundreds of accounts), consider scripting POST calls in a loop using a CSV or spreadsheet as the source of truth. Each POST creates one entry — there is no bulk import endpoint.

## Account Groups

_Reference: [Account Groups Endpoint](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-account-groups-end-point)_

Account Groups and Account Group Entries together provide a lightweight tagging system for cloud accounts **within Cloudability** — independent of native cloud tags. They allow you to organize accounts by any dimension meaningful to your organization (e.g., Team, Cost Center, Environment, Application) and then use those dimensions across all Cloudability reporting.

### Structure

- **Account Group** (201) — defines the **key/dimension name** (e.g., `"Environment"`)
- **Account Group Entry** (202) — assigns a **value** to a specific cloud account within a group (e.g., `"Production"` for AWS account `123456789012`)

### High-Level Workflow

1. Create one or more **Account Groups** (keys) — section 201
2. Create **Account Group Entries** for each group to tag individual cloud accounts — section 202
3. The Account Group names then appear as filterable/groupable dimensions throughout Cloudability reports and dashboards

### Permissions

- **Admins only** can create, update, and delete Account Groups and Entries via the UI and API
- All users can filter and group by Account Group dimensions in dashboards and reports

---

### Account Group Size Considerations

The Cloudability API documentation does not specify a maximum number of Account Group Entries per group. For organizations with large cloud portfolios, keep the following in mind:

**Recommendations for Large Account Lists**

- **Test with a subset first** -- before bulk-loading all account entries, test with 10-50 entries and verify response times and correctness
- **Expect large payloads on reads** -- the Account Group Entries endpoint returns all entries for a group in a single response; for groups with hundreds of entries, response payload size can become significant
- **Batch POST operations** -- when creating entries for 100+ accounts, consider batching in groups of 25-50 with a short pause between batches to avoid rate limiting
- **Retrieve before bulk updates** -- always fetch the current entry list before any bulk create or delete operation to avoid duplicates
- **Handle rate limiting** -- the Cloudability API enforces rate limits on write operations. If you receive `429 Too Many Requests` responses, implement exponential back-off in your automation

If you encounter consistent issues with large Account Group operations, contact IBM Cloudability support to confirm any limits specific to your account tier.

request.description:
**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/users`

Returns all users in the Cloudability organization. Use this to retrieve user IDs and current settings before making updates, or to audit user configurations such as default views and shared dimension filter sets.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |
| `Accept` | `application/json` |

### Response Fields (per user)

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `id` | Unique identifier for the user — use this as `{userid}` in the Update User call |
| `email` | The user's email address |
| `full_name` | The user's display name |
| `default_dimension_filter_set_id` | ID of the View currently set as this user's default |
| `shared_dimension_filter_set_ids` | Array of View IDs shared with this user |
| `role` | The user's Cloudability role (`admin`, `power_user`, `standard_user`, etc.) |

_Record user `id` values for use in the **Update User** call._

**PUT** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/users/{userid}`

Updates a user's display name, default View, or shared View assignments. This is the primary way to programmatically manage user View access — particularly useful for provisioning new users or bulk-updating View assignments after a Views reorganization.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |
| `Accept` | `application/json` |

### Path Parameter

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `{userid}` | The unique `id` of the user to update. Retrieve it from **Get Users** | `abc123` |

### Request Body Fields

| Field | Required | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `full_name` | No | Update the user's display name | `"Joan Doe"` |
| `default_dimension_filter_set_id` | No | Set the user's default View (by View ID from section 400) | `12` |
| `new_shared_dimension_filter_set_ids` | No | **Replace** the full list of View IDs shared with this user | `[12, 999]` |

> ⚠️ `new_shared_dimension_filter_set_ids` is a **full replacement** of the user's shared views list. Include all View IDs you want the user to have access to — any omitted IDs will be removed.

### View IDs

View IDs can be retrieved from the **400 Views** section. Use `viewid=0` in reports to override a user's default view and see all data.

**POST** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/users`

Creates a new user in the Cloudability organization. This call provisions a user record and optionally sets their default View and shared Views at creation time.

> **SSO / SAML Organizations -- Important:** If your Cloudability organization authenticates via **Single Sign-On (SSO) or SAML** through IBM Frontdoor (w3id, Azure AD, Okta, etc.), user accounts are managed by your identity provider. **This endpoint is not available for SSO-managed organizations.** User provisioning must be handled at the IdP level. This call applies only to organizations using **Cloudability-native authentication**.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |

### Required Permission

The calling user must have the **UserManagementFeatureFullAccess** permission.

### Request Body Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `email` | string | Yes | User's Frontdoor email address |
| `full_name` | string | Yes | Display name shown in user lists |
| `shared_dimension_filter_set_id` | integer | No | Default View ID for this user (`0` = all data view) |
| `new_shared_dimension_filter_set_ids` | array | No | Array of View IDs the user can access (full replacement of shared views list) |

### Example Request Body

```json
{
  "email": "jane.doe@example.com",
  "full_name": "Jane Doe",
  "shared_dimension_filter_set_id": 0,
  "new_shared_dimension_filter_set_ids": [1234, 5678]
}
```

### Notes

- Use **Get Views** (section 400) to retrieve valid View IDs before setting them here
- `new_shared_dimension_filter_set_ids` is a **full replacement** -- include all View IDs the user should have access to
- After creation, the user receives an invitation email to complete account setup
- _Reference: [Users End Point](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-users-end-point)_

Permanently removes a user from the Cloudability organization. The user immediately loses all access to Cloudability dashboards, reports, and APIs. This action cannot be undone.

> **SSO / SAML Organizations -- Important:** If your organization uses SSO/SAML through IBM Frontdoor, removing a user here only removes their Cloudability record -- it does **not** revoke their IdP session or Frontdoor access. For SSO orgs, always deprovision the user at the IdP level first, then optionally call this endpoint to clean up the Cloudability record.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Required Permission

The calling user must have the **UserManagementFeatureFullAccess** permission.

### Path Parameter

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `:userId` | The Cloudability integer user ID | `12345` |

### Workflow

1. Call **Get Users** to retrieve the user list
2. Find the user by `email` or `full_name`
3. Copy the integer `id` field
4. Replace `:userId` in the URL and execute

### Notes

- Deleting a user does **not** delete Budgets, Views, or Account Groups they created -- those resources persist under their original IDs
- If the deleted user was the sole owner of a Budget, that budget becomes ownerless -- reassign budget ownership before deleting the user if this matters to your workflow
- _Reference: [Users End Point](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-users-end-point)_

item.description:
## Users

_Reference: [Users Endpoint](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-users-end-point)_

The Users endpoint allows Cloudability admins to retrieve user information and programmatically manage user settings — primarily **View assignments** (default and shared Views).

### Key Use Cases

- **Audit user View access** — retrieve all users and their current default/shared View IDs
- **Bulk update Views** — after creating or reorganizing Views, update multiple users' access via API rather than the UI
- **Provision new users** — set the default View and shared Views immediately after a user is created
- **Rename users** — update display names programmatically

### Workflow

1. **Get Users** — retrieve all users and their current `id`, `full_name`, and View assignments
2. **Get Views** (section 400) — retrieve View IDs to use in user updates
3. **Update User** — set a user's default View, shared Views, or display name

### Permissions

- Only **Cloudability Admins** can read and update user records via the API
- View IDs used in user updates must exist — reference section 400 to retrieve valid View IDs

### Note on `new_shared_dimension_filter_set_ids`

This field is a **full replacement** of the user's shared View list. Always include every View ID you want the user to retain access to.

### SSO / SAML Organization Note

> If your organization uses **SSO or SAML authentication** through IBM Frontdoor, user creation and deletion must be managed at the identity provider level. The **Create User** and **Delete User** calls in this section are only functional for organizations using Cloudability-native authentication. See each call's description for full details.

item.name: 400 Views

request.description:
**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/views`

Returns all Views defined in the Cloudability instance. Views control the scope of cloud cost data visible to users — they can restrict by account, tag, service, or any dimension, and can be shared with specific users or the entire organization.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Response Fields (per View)

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `id` | Unique identifier for the View — use in PUT, DELETE, and user assignment calls |
| `title` | Display name of the View as seen by end users |
| `sharedWithOrganization` | `true` if visible to all users; `false` if restricted to specific users |
| `sharedWithUsers` | Array of user IDs this View is explicitly shared with (when not org-wide) |
| `ownerId` | ID of the user who created the View |
| `filters` | Array of filter objects that define the scope of the View |

### Filter Object Fields

| Field | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `field` | The dimension to filter on | `"vendor"`, `"account_identifier"`, `"tag1"` |
| `comparator` | The comparison operator | `"=="`, `"!="`, `"=~"` (regex) |
| `value` | The value to filter by | `"Amazon"`, `"123456789012"` |

_Note: This endpoint does not support server-side filtering or sorting of results._

variable.description: Cloudability View ID string -- retrieve from Get Views

request.description:
**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/views/:viewId`

Retrieves the full definition of a single View by its ID, including all filter rules, sharing settings, and owner details. Use this before updating a View to inspect its current state, or to validate a View ID before assigning it to a user.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Path Parameter

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `:viewId` | The Cloudability View ID string | `1234` |

### How to Find a View ID

1. Call **Get Views** to retrieve all Views
2. Locate the View by `title`
3. Use the `id` string value as `:viewId`

### Example Response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "id": "1234",
    "title": "Team Alpha - AWS",
    "sharedWithOrganization": false,
    "sharedWithUsers": ["567", "890"],
    "ownerId": "42",
    "filters": [
      {
        "dimension": "vendor",
        "operator": "==",
        "value": "aws"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Notes

- Use `view_id=0` in Cost Reporting and Rightsizing calls to bypass all Views and return all data (admin only)
- A View with no filters defined returns all data the requesting user has access to
- _Reference: [Views End Point](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-views-end-point)_

**POST** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/views`

Creates a new View. A View defines a scoped subset of cloud cost data (via filters) and controls which users can access it. Views are the primary mechanism for cost visibility governance in Cloudability.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Request Body Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | Yes | Display name for the View |
| `sharedWithOrganization` | Yes | `true` to share with all users; `false` to restrict to `sharedWithUsers` |
| `sharedWithUsers` | No | Array of user IDs to share with (when `sharedWithOrganization` is `false`) |
| `filters` | No | Array of filter objects scoping the data visible in this View |

### Filter Object Fields

| Field | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `field` | Dimension to filter on | `"vendor"`, `"account_identifier"`, `"tag1"` |
| `comparator` | Comparison operator | `"=="` (equals), `"!="` (not equals), `"=~"` (regex match) |
| `value` | Value to match | `"Amazon"`, `"123456789012"` |

### Filter Logic

- Multiple filters on the **same dimension** are combined with **OR**
- Multiple filters on **different dimensions** are combined with **AND**

### Example: Create an AWS-only View

```json
{
  "title": "AWS Only",
  "sharedWithOrganization": false,
  "sharedWithUsers": ["user-id-1", "user-id-2"],
  "filters": [{"field": "vendor", "comparator": "==", "value": "Amazon"}]
}
```

_The new View's `id` is returned in the response — record it for user assignment calls (section 300)._

**PUT** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/views/{viewid}`

Fully replaces an existing View's configuration. Use this to update the View's title, filter rules, or sharing settings.

> ⚠️ **This is a full replacement.** All filter rules are overwritten. Include the complete desired filter array in the request body.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Path Variable

| Variable | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `{{viewid}}` | The unique `id` of the View to update. Retrieve from **Get Views** | `"abc-123"` |

### Request Body Fields

Same fields as Create View: `title`, `sharedWithOrganization`, `sharedWithUsers`, `filters`. Include all fields — omitted fields revert to defaults.

**DELETE** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/views/{viewid}`

Permanently deletes a View. Any users whose default or shared Views reference this View ID will lose that assignment.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Path Variable

| Variable | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `{{viewid}}` | The `id` of the View to delete. Retrieve from **Get Views** | `"abc-123"` |

_Before deleting a View, use **300 Users** to check if any users have it set as their default or shared view, and re-assign them if needed._

item.description:
## Views

_Reference: [Views Endpoint](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-views-end-point)_

Cloudability **Views** are scoped data filters that control which cloud cost and usage data is visible to a given user or group. They are the primary access control mechanism for cost visibility — each user sees cost data through the lens of their assigned View.

A View can:
- Restrict visibility to specific accounts, vendors, tags, regions, or any dimension
- Be shared with specific users or the entire organization
- Be set as a user's **default View** (applied automatically when they log in or run a report)

### Views Object Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Unique identifier — use in PUT, DELETE, and user assignment calls |
| `title` | string | Display name shown to end users |
| `sharedWithOrganization` | boolean | `true` = visible to all users |
| `sharedWithUsers` | array | List of user IDs with explicit access |
| `ownerId` | string | User ID of the View creator |
| `filters` | array | Filter rules defining the data scope |

### Filter Logic

- Filters on the **same dimension** → combined with **OR**
- Filters on **different dimensions** → combined with **AND**

### Workflow

1. **Get Views** — list all Views and find their `id` values
2. **Create View** — define a new scoped View with filter rules
3. **Update Views** — modify an existing View's filters or sharing (full overwrite)
4. **Delete Views** — permanently remove a View
5. Use View IDs with **300 Users** to assign Views to users
6. Use `view_id=0` in Cost Reporting and other endpoints to bypass user Views and see all data (admin only)

_Note: This endpoint does not support server-side filtering or sorting of the View list._

## Forecast

_Reference: [Forecast Endpoint](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-forecast-end-point)_

The Forecast section provides two complementary spend projection capabilities:

| Call | Endpoint | What it returns |
|---|---|---|
| Get Current Month Estimate | `/v3/estimate` | A single projected total for the **current calendar month** based on spend to date |
| Get Forecast | `/v3/forecast` | A **multi-month forecast** using linear regression on historical spend data |

### Key Concepts

- **Cost Basis:** All forecast calls support multiple cost bases (`cash`, `amortized`, `adjusted`, etc.) — choose the basis that aligns with your organization's financial reporting
- **ViewId:** Use `viewId=0` for all data (admin), or specify a View ID to scope the forecast to a subset of accounts
- **CSV Output:** The Get Forecast call supports `Accept: text/csv` for direct export (header is disabled by default — enable it to switch to CSV)

### Forecast Modeling Notes

- The forecast uses **linear regression** on `monthsBack` months of historical actuals
- Credits and one-time charges can distort the trend line — use `removeCredits=true` and `removeOneTimeCharges=true` for cleaner baseline modeling
- Setting `useCurrentEstimate=true` includes the current month's partial-month estimate in the model

## Budget Subscriptions

_Reference: [Budgets Endpoint](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-budgets-end-point)_

Budget Subscriptions control **email alert delivery** for a budget. A subscription opts the authenticated user into alerts for a specific budget — independently of other users.

### Alert Types

| Alert | Field | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Forecast alert | `notifyExpected: true` | Email sent when Cloudability forecasts spend will exceed the monthly threshold |
| Exceeded alert | `notifyExceeded: true` | Email sent when actual spend has already exceeded the monthly threshold |

### Important Notes

- Subscriptions are **per-user** — each user manages their own subscription independently
- The budget must exist before creating a subscription (use section 601)
- Deleting a budget (601 Delete) also removes all associated subscriptions
- Deleting a subscription does **not** delete the underlying budget

### Workflow

1. **Get All Subscriptions** — list existing alert subscriptions for the current user
2. **Create Budget Subscriptions** — opt in to alerts for a specific budget
3. **Update Budget Subscription** — change which alert types are active
4. **Delete Budget Subscription** — opt out of alerts for a specific budget

## Budgets

_Reference: [Budgets Endpoint](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-budgets-end-point)_

This section covers the complete Budget management workflow in Cloudability:

| Sub-folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| 601 Budgets | CRUD operations for budget definitions and monthly thresholds |
| 602 Budget Subscriptions | Per-user email alert subscriptions for budget threshold notifications |

### How Budgets Work

1. A **Budget** defines monthly spend thresholds for a given cost basis and View scope
2. Cloudability evaluates actual spend against those thresholds each month
3. **Budget Subscriptions** determine which users receive email alerts and which alert types they receive (forecast vs. exceeded)
4. Alerts are delivered by email when thresholds are projected to be or are actually breached

### Key Notes

- Budget IDs are **UUIDs** (e.g., `d090e29e-2a26-4ca5-7f9a-67be3134081e`)
- The `Accept: text/csv` header is available on all calls in this section but disabled by default
- Budgets are scoped to a View (`viewId`) — use `"0"` for all data
- PUT on a budget is a full overwrite of the months array

---

### Budget Alert Threshold Behavior

Understanding how Cloudability evaluates and delivers budget alerts helps you configure subscriptions correctly and set appropriate expectations.

**Evaluation Frequency**
- Cloudability evaluates budget thresholds **once per day**, typically during overnight processing
- Alerts are triggered when actual spend or the forecasted end-of-month spend meets or exceeds the monthly `threshold` value

**Alert Types (the `alertType` field on Budget Subscription objects)**

| Alert Type | Trigger Condition |
|---|---|
| `forecastAlert` | Cloudability's forecasting engine projects that spend will **exceed** the monthly threshold before month end |
| `exceedAlert` | Actual spend has already **exceeded** the monthly threshold |

**Alert Frequency -- Once Per Month Per Subscription Per Type**
- Budget threshold alerts are sent **at most once per billing month** per subscription per alert type
- If you receive a `forecastAlert` on the 10th and the forecast still shows overage on the 11th, you will **not** receive a second alert -- Cloudability suppresses repeat notifications for the same threshold within the same calendar month
- A new alert cycle begins at the start of each new calendar month

**Threshold Evaluation Logic**
- The `threshold` value on each month object is a **dollar amount** (not a percentage)
- Cloudability compares this dollar amount against the selected `basis` (e.g., `amortized`, `cash`) for the matching calendar month
- Months without an explicit entry in the `months` array generate no alert for that period -- set a threshold for every month you want to monitor
- Setting `threshold` to `0` disables alerting for that month

**Practical Configuration Recommendations**
- Use `forecastAlert` as an early warning signal (typically triggers mid-month when forecast confidence is high)
- Use `exceedAlert` as a hard-stop notification (triggers when actual spend crosses the threshold)
- To receive both early warning and confirmed alerts, create **two subscriptions** on the same budget -- one with `alertType: forecastAlert` and one with `alertType: exceedAlert`
- For multi-team budgets, create one subscription per user using their Cloudability user ID in the `userId` field

### Tag and Business Dimension Naming Conventions

| Dimension Pattern | What it refers to |
|---|---|
| `tag1`, `tag2`, `tag4`, … `tagN` | Native vendor tag keys, indexed by Cloudability. The mapping of tag key names to index numbers is shown in **Get Cost Measures**. |
| `category1`, `category2`, `category3`, … | Business Dimensions from section 100, indexed by their `index` value. `category2` = the Business Mapping with `index: 2`. |

### The `filters` Parameter

Filters narrow the data returned by the report. Each filter is a string in the format `{dimension}{operator}{value}`:

| Operator | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `==` | Equals | `tag4==morphius` |
| `!=` | Not equals | `vendor!=Microsoft` |
| `>` | Greater than | `unblended_cost>100` |
| `<` | Less than | `unblended_cost<1000` |
| `=@` | Contains | `account_name=@production` |
| `!=(not set)` | Field has a value (is not empty) | `instance_type!=(not set)` |

**Multiple filters:** Add a separate `filters=` parameter for each filter. Multiple filters are AND-combined.

### This Example

Returns last month's total amortized cost grouped by native tag #4 (where value = 'morphius'), Business Dimension #2, and Business Dimension #3.
