**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/reporting/cost/run` _(with pagination)_

Demonstrates cursor-based pagination for large reports that exceed 10,000 rows. Use `limit` to set the page size and `token` to navigate between pages.

### Pagination Parameters

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | Number of rows per page. Default: 500. Maximum: 10,000 | `limit=500` |
| `token` | Pagination cursor. Empty string for the first page; the `next` token value from the previous response for subsequent pages | `token=abc123xyz` |

### How Pagination Works

1. Make the first request with `limit=N` and `token=` (empty)
2. The response includes a `pagination` object with a `next` field
3. If `next` is non-null, there are more rows — copy the `next` value and use it as the `token` value in the next request
4. Repeat until `next` is null (last page)

### Example Pagination Response

```json
{
  "results": [...],
  "pagination": {
    "next": "eyJvZmZzZXQiOjUwfQ==",
    "total": 12500
  }
}
```

_For very large reports (millions of rows), consider using the **Run Report as Enqueue** approach instead, which processes the report asynchronously._

**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/reporting/cost/enqueue`

Submits a report for **asynchronous processing**. Instead of waiting for the report to complete (as with `/run`), this endpoint immediately returns an `id` that you use to retrieve the results once processing is complete. This is the recommended approach for large reports.

### When to Use Enqueue vs. Run

| Scenario | Use |
|---|---|
| Small/medium reports (< 100k rows) | `/run` — synchronous, results returned immediately |
| Large reports (100k+ rows) | `/enqueue` → poll `/reports/{id}/results` |
| Scheduled/automated reports | `/enqueue` — avoids timeout issues |

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Query Parameters

Same parameters as `/run`: `start_date`, `end_date`, `dimensions`, `metrics`, `filters`, `sort`, `view_id`.

### Response

Returns an object with an `id` field — the report job ID. Store this and use it in **Enqueue Results from ID**.

### Test Script

This collection automatically captures the report ID:

``` javascript
var jsonData = JSON.parse(responseBody);
postman.setEnvironmentVariable("enqueueID", jsonData.id);
```

### Report Status Values

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pending` | Report is queued |
| `running` | Report is being processed |
| `complete` | Results are ready — call **Enqueue Results from ID** |
| `failed` | An error occurred during processing |

variable.description: Enqueue job ID returned from the POST /enqueue call

request.description:
**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/reporting/cost/enqueue/:enqueueId`

Checks the status of an asynchronous enqueued cost report job. After submitting a report via **Run Report as Enqueue** (POST to `/enqueue`), poll this endpoint until the status returns `complete` before fetching results.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Path Parameter

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `:enqueueId` | The enqueue job ID returned by the POST `/enqueue` call | `a1b2c3d4-1234-5678-abcd-ef1234567890` |

### Job Status Values

| Status | Meaning | Next Action |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` | Job is queued and waiting to be processed | Poll again in 5-10 seconds |
| `processing` | Job is currently running | Poll again in 5-10 seconds |
| `complete` | Job finished successfully -- results are ready | Call **Enqueue Results from ID** to fetch data |
| `failed` | Job failed -- results are not available | Review parameters and resubmit |

### Polling Workflow

```
1. POST /v3/reporting/cost/enqueue         -> returns enqueueId
2. GET  /v3/reporting/cost/enqueue/:id     -> check status
3. If status == "pending" or "processing"  -> wait 5-10s, repeat step 2
4. If status == "complete"                 -> GET /v3/reporting/cost/enqueue/:id/results
5. If status == "failed"                   -> review parameters and resubmit
```

### Example Response (complete)

```json
{
  "result": {
    "id": "a1b2c3d4-1234-5678-abcd-ef1234567890",
    "status": "complete",
    "createdAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
    "completedAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:45Z"
  }
}
```

### Notes

- Very large reports may take several minutes to process -- design your polling loop accordingly
- Use a reasonable back-off interval (5-30 seconds) rather than tight polling to avoid rate limiting
- The enqueue job ID is returned in the `result.id` field of the POST `/enqueue` response -- capture this before polling
- _Reference: [Cost Reporting End Point](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-cost-reporting-end-point)_

**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/reporting/reports/{enqueueID}/results`

Retrieves the results of an asynchronously enqueued report. Call this after **Run Report as Enqueue Example** returns a report `id`. Poll this endpoint until the status is `complete`, then read the results.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Path Variable

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `{{enqueueID}}` | The report job ID returned by **Run Report as Enqueue**. Automatically stored as an environment variable by that call's test script. |

- If status is `pending` or `running`: returns a status object — wait and retry
- If status is `complete`: returns the full report results in the same format as `/run`
- If status is `failed`: returns an error message

### Polling Recommendation

Wait 5–30 seconds between poll attempts depending on report size. Most reports complete within 60 seconds. Very large reports may take several minutes.

_Once results are retrieved, they may be available for a limited time before expiring — process and store them promptly._

item.description:
## Cost Reporting

_Reference: [Cost Reporting Endpoint](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-cost-reporting-end-point)_

The Cost Reporting section provides access to Cloudability's core cost and usage reporting API. Reports are built by specifying dimensions (grouping fields), metrics (numeric measures), date ranges, filters, and sort order.

### Calls in This Section

| Call | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Get Cost Measures | Discover all valid dimension and metric names for your instance |
| Basic Cost Report (Required Params) | Minimal working report — vendor/account breakdown |
| Basic Cost Report - CSV Return | Same report but returned as CSV via `Accept: text/csv` |
| Simple View/Sort Example | Demonstrates `sort` and `view_id` parameters |
| Tag and Business Mapping Example | Using native tags (`tag#`) and Business Dimensions (`category#`) with `filters` |
| Combining Multiple Filters Example | Multiple AND-combined filter conditions |
| Container Cost Allocation Report | Container-specific dimensions and metrics |
| Limit Parameter w/ Pagination | Cursor-based pagination for large result sets |
| Run Report as Enqueue | Asynchronous report submission for very large reports |
| Enqueue Results from ID | Retrieve results of an enqueued report |

### Required Parameters (for `/run` and `/enqueue`)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `start_date` | Report start — ISO date (`2024-01-01`) or relative expression (`beginning of last month`) |
| `end_date` | Report end — ISO date or relative expression |
| `dimensions` | Comma-separated grouping fields |
| `metrics` | Comma-separated numeric measures |

### Optional Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `filters` | One per filter condition, AND-combined. Format: `{dimension}{operator}{value}` |
| `sort` | `{metricName}ASC` or `{metricName}DESC` |
| `view_id` | Scope to a View. `0` = all data (admin only) |
| `limit` | Rows per page (default 500, max 10,000) |
| `token` | Pagination cursor for next page |

### CSV Output

Add `Accept: text/csv` to any `/run` or `/enqueue` call to receive results as CSV.

### Business Dimensions in Reports

Business Dimensions (from section 100) are referenced as `category{index}` — e.g., `category2` for the mapping with `index: 2`. Native vendor tags are referenced as `tag{index}` — use **Get Cost Measures** to find the index for a specific tag key name.

---

### Standard Dimensions Reference

Use **Get Cost Measures** to retrieve the exact dimension names valid for your Cloudability instance. The following standard dimensions are available across most configurations:

| API Name | Display Name | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `vendor` | Cloud Vendor | Values: `aws`, `azure`, `gcp` |
| `account_name` | Account Name | Cloud account display name |
| `account_identifier` | Account ID | AWS account number, Azure subscription ID, GCP project ID |
| `region` | Region | Cloud region (e.g., `us-east-1`, `eastus`) |
| `service_name` | Service | Cloud service family (e.g., `Amazon EC2`, `Azure Virtual Machines`) |
| `enhanced_service_name` | Enhanced Service | More granular service grouping |
| `usage_family` | Usage Type | Category within a service (e.g., `BoxUsage`, `DataTransfer`) |
| `resource_identifier` | Resource ID | Individual resource ID when available |
| `resource_type` | Resource Type | Instance/SKU type (e.g., `m5.large`, `Standard_D4s_v3`) |
| `operation` | Operation | Specific API operation billed |
| `availability_zone` | Availability Zone | AZ within a region |
| `invoice_item_description` | Line Item Description | Raw billing line-item description from the cloud provider |
| `pricing_model` | Pricing Model | `On-Demand`, `Savings Plan`, `Reserved`, `Spot` |
| `legal_entity` | Legal Entity | AWS only -- first-party vs. marketplace charges |
| `month` | Month | Billing month in `YYYY-MM` format |
| `week` | Week | ISO week |
| `day` | Day | Calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) |
| `year` | Year | Calendar year |
| `project_name` | Project | GCP project name |
| `category{N}` | Business Dimension N | Business Dimension at index N (see section 100 Business Mappings) |
| `tag{N}` | Tag N | Native vendor tag at index N -- use Get Cost Measures to find the index for a specific tag key |

### Tag Dimensions

Native vendor tags are referenced as `tag{N}` where `N` is the tag's index number in your Cloudability instance. Use **Get Cost Measures** to map tag key names to their index numbers. For example, if the `Environment` tag is at index 3, use `tag3` as the dimension name in reports and filters.

### Business Dimensions

Business Dimensions created in section 100 appear as `category{N}` where `N` is the `index` value on the Business Mapping object. For example, a Business Mapping with `"index": 2` is referenced as `category2` in reports, filters, and sorts.

### Container Dimensions

For container cost allocation reports, the following additional dimensions are available:

| API Name | Description |
|---|---|
| `cluster_name` | Kubernetes or ECS cluster name |
| `namespace` | Kubernetes namespace |
| `workload_name` | Kubernetes workload name (Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, etc.) |
| `container_name` | Container name within a pod |
| `label{N}` | Kubernetes label at index N -- use Get Cost Measures for the index |

---

### Filter Operators Reference

The `filters` query parameter uses a `{dimension}{operator}{value}` format. The complete list of supported operators is available from the API itself at `GET /v3/reporting/cost/filters`. The full operator set is:

| Operator | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `==` | Equals (case-sensitive exact match) | `vendor==aws` |
| `===` | Strictly equals (reserved for numeric fields) | `total_cost===100` |
| `!=` | Not equals | `vendor!=azure` |
| `!==` | Strictly not equals (numeric) | `total_cost!==0` |
| `=@` | Contains (substring match) | `region=@us-east` |
| `!=@` | Does not contain | `resource_identifier!=@test` |
| `>` | Greater than (numeric dimensions and metrics) | `total_amortized_cost>100` |
| `>=` | Greater than or equal to | `total_amortized_cost>=500` |
| `<` | Less than | `total_amortized_cost<50` |
| `<=` | Less than or equal to | `total_amortized_cost<=1000` |
| `[]==` | In set (value is one of a comma-separated list) | `vendor[]==aws,azure` |
| `[]!=` | Not in set | `region[]!=us-east-1,eu-west-1` |

### Filter Syntax Rules

- Each `filters=` parameter is one condition -- use **multiple** `filters=` parameters to AND conditions together
- Filters on the **same dimension** are evaluated as **OR** within that dimension
- Filters on **different dimensions** are evaluated as **AND** across dimensions
- URL-encode operators when building requests manually: `==` becomes `%3D%3D`, `=@` becomes `%3D%40`, `>` becomes `%3E`
- String values are **case-sensitive** by default -- use the `=@` contains operator for case-insensitive partial matching

### Live Operator Discovery

Retrieve the live operator list for your Cloudability instance:

```
GET https://api.cloudability.com/v3/reporting/cost/filters
```

This returns the exact operator strings recognized by your version of Cloudability, which is the authoritative source if operators change across versions.

### Filter Examples

```
# Vendor equals AWS
filters=vendor==aws

# Region contains "east"
filters=region=@east

# Amortized cost greater than $100
filters=total_amortized_cost>100

# Tag "Environment" equals "Production"  (tag3 = Environment in your instance)
filters=tag3==Production

# Multiple AND filters: AWS AND us-east-1
filters=vendor==aws&filters=region==us-east-1

# In-set: AWS or Azure only
filters=vendor[]==aws,azure
```

**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/rightsizing/azure/recommendations/sql`

Returns Azure SQL Database rightsizing recommendations filtered by a tag value and resource name. Demonstrates rightsizing-specific filter syntax.

### Rightsizing `filters` Syntax

Rightsizing filters use a **comma-separated** list within a single `filters=` parameter (unlike Cost Reporting which uses multiple `filters=` parameters):

```
filters=tag7==it%26s,name=@kia
```

### Rightsizing Filter Operators

| Operator | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `==` | Equals | `tag7==production` |
| `!=` | Not equals | `recommendations.action!=Rightsize` |
| `=@` | Contains | `name=@webserver` |
| `>` | Greater than | `recommendations.savings>50` |

### Special Characters in Filters

URL-encode special characters in filter values:
- `&` → `%26`
- `=` → `%3D`
- `(` → `%28`, `)` → `%29`

### Filtering on Recommendation Attributes

Prefix with `recommendations.` to filter on properties of the recommendation itself:
- `recommendations.action==Rightsize`
- `recommendations.savings>100`
- `recommendations.defaultsOrder==1` (matches the default/top recommendation)

**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/rightsizing/aws/recommendations/ec2`

Returns AWS EC2 instance rightsizing recommendations. Cloudability analyzes CloudWatch (or third-party) utilization metrics to identify over-provisioned instances and recommend right-sized alternatives.

### Required Parameters

| Parameter | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `basis` | Cost basis for savings calculations | `on-demand`, `effective` |
| `duration` | Utilization look-back period | `ten-day`, `thirty-day` |
| `limit` | Results per page | Integer |
| `offset` | Pagination start (0-based) | Integer |

### Optional Parameters

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `vendorAccountIds` | Filter to specific AWS accounts (comma-separated) | `123456789012,987654321098` |
| `filters` | Comma-separated rightsizing filters | `recommendations.defaultsOrder==1` |
| `maxRecsPerResource` | Max recommendations per instance (default 1) | `5` |
| `sort` | Sort field with `-` prefix for descending | `-recommendations.savings` |
| `source` | Utilization data source | `cloudwatch`, `datadog` |
| `viewId` | View scope (`0` = all data) | `0` |
| `rank` | Ranking method for compute products | `default` |

### The `recommendations.defaultsOrder==1` Filter

This filter (URL-encoded as `recommendations.defaultsOrder%3D%3D1`) limits results to the single top-ranked recommendation per instance — equivalent to what the Cloudability UI shows by default.

**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/rightsizing/aws/recommendations/lambda`

Returns rightsizing recommendations for **AWS Lambda functions**. Analyzes peak memory consumption versus allocated memory to identify functions where allocated memory can be safely reduced, lowering per-invocation costs.

### Prerequisites

Before Lambda recommendations will appear, the following must be in place:

1. The AWS IAM role used by Cloudability must include the `lambda:ListFunctions` and `lambda:ListProvisionedConcurrencyConfigs` permissions
2. **AWS Lambda Insights** must be enabled for the functions you want to monitor -- without it, memory utilization data is unavailable and no recommendations will be generated
3. Allow 24-72 hours after enabling Lambda Insights for utilization data to appear in Cloudability

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Query Parameters

All parameters are disabled by default -- enable what you need.

| Parameter | Description | Example Values |
|---|---|---|
| `basis` | Cost basis for savings calculations | `on-demand` (only supported value for Lambda) |
| `duration` | Look-back period for utilization analysis | `seven-day`, `thirty-day` |
| `limit` | Max results per page | `25` |
| `offset` | Pagination offset | `0` |
| `sort` | Sort field and direction | `-recommendations.savings` (descending by savings) |
| `viewId` | Scope results to a View | `0` (all data) |
| `maxRecsPerResource` | Max recommendations per function | `1` (returns top recommendation only) |
| `filters` | Filter results by field | `resourceIdentifier==my-function-name` |

### Lambda-Specific Notes

- Lambda rightsizing is based on **peak memory** observed during the look-back period, not average memory
- Cloudability recommends reducing allocated memory to a value above the observed peak, with a safety margin
- Lambda does **not** support the `effective` cost basis -- use `on-demand` only
- Functions with very short execution times or low invocation counts may not have enough data for a recommendation
- _Reference: [AWS Rightsizing](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=cloudability-aws-rightsizing)_

**GET** `https://api.cloudability.com/v3/rightsizing/aws/recommendations/elasticip`

Returns recommendations to **terminate unattached AWS Elastic IP addresses**. Elastic IPs that are not associated with a running EC2 instance or network interface incur a small hourly charge. Cloudability identifies these idle EIPs and recommends releasing them.

> **Added:** This endpoint was added to Cloudability on January 9, 2026. If you do not see results, verify your Cloudability subscription includes this resource type.

### No Additional IAM Permissions Required

Unlike Lambda, no new AWS IAM permissions are needed for ElasticIP recommendations. Cloudability can identify unattached EIPs using the existing billing data already ingested.

### Required Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `apptio-opentoken` | `{{apptio-opentoken}}` |
| `apptio-current-environment` | `{{apptio-current-environment}}` |

### Query Parameters

All parameters are disabled by default -- enable what you need.

| Parameter | Description | Example Values |
|---|---|---|
| `basis` | Cost basis | `on-demand` |
| `duration` | Look-back period | `thirty-day` |
| `limit` | Max results per page | `25` |
| `offset` | Pagination offset | `0` |
| `sort` | Sort field and direction | `-recommendations.savings` |
| `viewId` | Scope results to a View | `0` (all data) |
| `vendorAccountIds` | Filter by AWS account number | `123456789012` |
| `filters` | Filter results | `region==us-east-1` |

### Recommendation Actions

| Action | Description |
|---|---|
| `Terminate` | Release the unattached Elastic IP address to stop incurring charges |

### AWS ElasticIP Pricing Note

AWS charges for Elastic IPs that are **not** associated with a running instance:
- ~$0.005/hour per unattached EIP (approximately $3.60/month each)
- While individually small, organizations with many unattached EIPs from previous deployments can accumulate meaningful waste

### Notes

- ElasticIP recommendations are **Terminate only** -- there is no rightsizing option for EIPs
- An EIP associated with a *stopped* instance still incurs charges and will appear in recommendations
- Use `filters=region==us-east-1` to scope results to a specific region
- _Reference: [AWS Rightsizing](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=cloudability-aws-rightsizing)_

## AWS Rightsizing

_Reference: [Rightsizing Endpoints](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-rightsizing-end-points)_

This sub-folder contains AWS-specific rightsizing calls for the products supported by Cloudability.

### Supported AWS Products

| Call | Endpoint | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| EC2 | `/rightsizing/aws/recommendations/ec2` | `basis=effective` available |
| EC2-ASG | `/rightsizing/aws/recommendations/ec2-asg` | Auto Scaling Group launch configs |
| EBS | `/rightsizing/aws/recommendations/ebs` | `basis=on-demand` only |
| S3 | `/rightsizing/aws/recommendations/s3` | `duration=thirty-day` only |
| RDS | `/rightsizing/aws/recommendations/rds` | `basis=effective` available; uses `preferenceOrder` filter |
| Redshift | `/rightsizing/aws/underutilized/redshift` | Different path and `basis=cost` |
| Lambda | `/rightsizing/aws/recommendations/lambda` | `on-demand` only; requires Lambda Insights |
| ElasticIP | `/rightsizing/aws/recommendations/elasticip` | Terminate only; no new IAM permissions needed |

### Required Parameters (all AWS products)

`basis`, `duration`, `limit`, `offset`

### The `effective` Cost Basis

Only available for **EC2** and **RDS**. When your environment has Reserved Instances or Savings Plans, use `basis=effective` for savings calculations that reflect your actual (discounted) costs.

---

### `fields` Parameter -- AWS Resource Types

The optional `fields` query parameter lets you limit the API response to specific columns, reducing payload size for large result sets. Append as a comma-separated list: `&fields=resourceIdentifier,accountName,recommendations.savings`

**Common Fields (available across all AWS resource types)**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `resourceIdentifier` | AWS Resource ID (instance ID, volume ID, function ARN, etc.) |
| `resourceName` | Name tag of the resource |
| `accountName` | AWS account display name |
| `accountIdentifier` | AWS account number (12 digits) |
| `region` | AWS region (e.g., `us-east-1`) |
| `totalCost` | Total cost over the look-back period |
| `recommendations.savings` | Estimated monthly savings from implementing the top recommendation |
| `recommendations.action` | Recommended action: `Rightsize`, `Terminate`, `Upgrade` |
| `recommendations.recommendedType` | Recommended instance or volume type |
| `idlePercentage` | Percentage of time the resource was idle during the look-back period |
| `tags` | Resource tags as key-value pairs |

**EC2-Specific Fields**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `currentType` | Current EC2 instance type (e.g., `m5.large`) |
| `cpuMax` | Max CPU utilization percentage over the period |
| `memoryMax` | Max memory utilization (requires CloudWatch agent on the instance) |
| `networkMax` | Max network I/O throughput |

**EBS-Specific Fields**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `volumeType` | Current EBS volume type (e.g., `gp2`, `gp3`, `io1`) |
| `volumeSize` | Current volume size in GB |
| `iopsMax` | Max IOPS utilization over the period |

**S3-Specific Fields**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `storageClass` | Current S3 storage class (e.g., `STANDARD`, `INTELLIGENT_TIERING`) |
| `storageSize` | Total bucket size in GB |
| `requestCount` | Total number of requests over the look-back period |

**RDS-Specific Fields**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `currentType` | Current RDS instance class (e.g., `db.m5.large`) |
| `cpuMax` | Max CPU utilization |
| `connectionMax` | Max database connections |
| `storageSize` | Allocated storage in GB |

**Lambda-Specific Fields**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `allocatedMemory` | Currently allocated memory in MB |
| `peakMemory` | Peak memory consumed during invocations |
| `recommendations.recommendedMemory` | Recommended memory allocation in MB |

## Container Rightsizing

_Reference: [Rightsizing Endpoints](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-rightsizing-end-points)_

This sub-folder contains rightsizing calls for **Kubernetes and container workloads** running on any supported cloud provider (AWS EKS, Azure AKS, GCP GKE, and self-managed clusters).

### Supported Container Resources

| Call | Endpoint | Resource Type |
|---|---|---|
| Workloads | `/rightsizing/containers/recommendations/workloads` | Kubernetes Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets |
| Namespaces | `/rightsizing/containers/recommendations/namespaces` | Namespace-level roll-up (availability tier-dependent) |
| Clusters | `/rightsizing/containers/recommendations/clusters` | Cluster-level roll-up (availability tier-dependent) |

### How Container Rightsizing Works

Cloudability analyzes CPU and memory **requests** and **limits** set on Kubernetes workload containers against actual observed utilization. Recommendations identify:

- **Over-provisioned** workloads where requests can be reduced (cost savings)
- **Under-provisioned** workloads where requests should be increased (reliability risk)
- Workloads where requests and limits are set to the same value (no burst headroom)

### Prerequisites

- Container cost allocation must be enabled in Cloudability (**Settings > Container Clusters**)
- The cluster must be registered and reporting utilization data
- Cloudability requires the container metrics agent to be installed on each cluster

### Relationship to the Rightsizing Examples Sub-folder

The **Container Workload Example** in the **Rightsizing Examples** sub-folder (at the top of section 800) demonstrates a specific filtered call. This sub-folder provides the full parameter set for production use.

### Notes

- Container rightsizing spans all cloud vendors -- use `filters=vendor==aws` etc. to scope to one provider
- `basis` is not applicable for containers -- container recommendations are based on CPU/memory resource units, not cost basis
- _Reference: [Rightsizing Endpoints](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-rightsizing-end-points)_

### Drill-Down Hierarchy

The three container calls form a natural drill-down hierarchy:

```
Clusters (highest-level overview)
  └── Namespaces (breakdown by namespace within a cluster)
        └── Workloads (individual Deployments/StatefulSets/DaemonSets)
```

Start with **Clusters** to identify the most wasteful clusters, then use **Namespaces** filtered by `clusterName` to pinpoint problem areas, then use **Workloads** filtered by `namespace` to find specific resources to right-size.

## Rightsizing

_Reference: [Rightsizing Endpoints](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloudability-commercial/cloudability-enterprise/saas?topic=api-rightsizing-end-points)_

The Rightsizing section provides access to Cloudability's compute, storage, and managed service rightsizing recommendations across AWS, Azure, and GCP. Recommendations are based on historical utilization data and compare current resource configurations against available alternatives to identify cost savings.

### Structure

| Sub-folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| Rightsizing Examples | Cross-vendor pattern examples (recommended starting point) |
| AWS | EC2, EC2-ASG, EBS, S3, RDS, Redshift |
| Azure | Compute (VMs), SQL Database, Managed Disk |
| GCP | GCE (Compute Engine), GDP (Persistent Disks) |

### Universal Required Parameters

| Parameter | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `basis` | Cost basis for savings calculations | `on-demand` (all); `effective` (EC2, RDS only) |
| `duration` | Utilization look-back period | `ten-day`, `thirty-day` (S3: thirty-day only) |
| `limit` | Results per page | Integer (default 50) |
| `offset` | Pagination start position | Integer (0-based, default 0) |

### Universal Optional Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `filters` | Comma-separated filter conditions (see Rightsizing Examples for syntax) |
| `maxRecsPerResource` | Max recommendations per resource (default 1) |
| `sort` | Sort field with `-` prefix for descending (default: `-recommendations.savings`) |
| `vendorAccountIds` | Comma-separated cloud account IDs to scope results |
| `viewId` | View ID scope (`0` = all data) |
| `source` | Utilization data source (`cloudwatch`, `datadog`, etc.) |

### Cost Basis Notes

- `on-demand`: Savings calculated at on-demand pricing — use when you have no RI/SP coverage
- `effective`: Savings calculated at your actual blended/RI rate — use when you have significant RI/SP coverage (available for **EC2** and **RDS** only)
- GCP always requires `on-demand`; `effective` is not supported

### CSV Output

Add `Accept: text/csv` header (currently disabled on all calls) to receive results as CSV.
